description:
The proposed development comprises a 6-metre rear extension, a full-height side extension, a loft conversion, and comprehensive internal refurbishment to reinstate the property as a contemporary family dwelling after an extended period of vacancy.

The existing street-facing elevation is currently in a state of disrepair and lacks coherence with the surrounding streetscape. The proposal seeks to improve visual harmony by introducing a new bay window within the side extension, echoing the vernacular character of neighbouring properties and establishing a balanced, symmetrical frontage.

The side elevation, partially visible from the public realm, will feature a refined composition of white render and vertical clay tile banding. These vertical elements introduce visual texture and help modulate the scale of the new volume, while also establishing a subtle architectural link with the adjacent property, The Crest, and referencing the traditional clay tiling found on existing bay windows.

To the rear, the proposal utilises the footprint established by the previous planning application (HGY/2025/0514), forming a pair of well-proportioned rooms oriented around an internal courtyard with a glazed roof. Expansive rooflights will deliver high levels of natural light to the rooms. A comprehensive daylight and sunlight assessment accompanies this application, demonstrating compliance with BRE guidance and ensuring optimal internal conditions year-round.  The assessment also demonstrates minimal impact to the neighbouring property at number 25 Ellington Road.

The garden stairs abut the boundary with number 25, this minimises any wall mass at the boundary to maximise the light levels to their property and creates a buffer zone at the boundary to limit overlooking.  A planter will be included along the glazed balustrade on the patio deck to further improve privacy.  The rear patio deck will be level with the ground level of The Crest, a suitable fence and planter will be installed to mitigate any privacy concerns.

The loft extension comprises three linked dormer volumes clad in charcoal-toned zinc, carefully positioned to maintain symmetry and minimise visual bulk.  The glazing is stepped back from the rear wall and boundaries to minimise any overlooking aspects. The principal roof slope will retain its original tiles and incorporate two new rooflights.  The cladding of the dormers continues through the rear of the house to delineate the glazing, providing a coherent, symmetrical design.

Collectively, the works have been designed to elevate the architectural character of the building and to improve the local streetscape.

The side extension will be constructed using timber framing to improve the eco-credentials of the building and minimise the construction time.  The roof dormers will hold PV panels, which will power a battery pack and an air-source heat pump.  The building will aim for zero natural gas usage.
